The day's crypto news is a mixture of market positioning, fund flows, policy updates, and company decisions. The headlines below are worth reading for the detail behind them, not just the reaction on a price chart.

What is moving the conversation

How a bug in Coldcard’s code went unnoticed for years, leading to $100 million in hacked funds. Crypto’s favorite maxim, “don’t trust, verify” wasn’t followed in the case of Coldcard’s code. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

No change in bitcoin holdings as Strategy boosted dollar reserve, bought back more STRC last week. Led by Executive Chairman Michael Saylor, the company raised $333.7 million via the sale of common stock. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Ethereum’s next big upgrade has 66 proposals, including a major privacy fix. Developers are narrowing the list for the Hegotá upgrade, including a package to change how wallets approve and pay for transactions, giving developers of privacy apps more of the tools they need inside Ethereum itself. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Israel’s largest crypto broker Bits of Gold hit by data breach affecting 200,000 customers. Funds and digital assets were not touched, but names, bank account details, and national ID numbers may have been exposed in what the company says was a wider global attack. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Bitcoin options remain expensive despite summer calm. Here's why it matters. Bitcoin’s implied volatility is near a seasonal floor, but options continue to price substantially more movement than the market is delivering. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Bitcoin's biggest holders, Strategy and Metaplanet, are betting on math, not price. Your day-ahead look for Aug. 17, 2026 Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Market context

Bitcoin is around $63,597 with a +0.94% 24-hour move, while Ether is around $1,902.51 with a +1.19% move. Those figures are a snapshot, not a forecast. The useful question is whether the move is supported by spot demand, volume, and a clear change in the news.

When the market is quiet, leverage and liquidity can matter as much as direction. A small headline can move price quickly when traders are positioned too closely on one side.

What to watch next

  • New ETF creations and redemptions.
  • Futures open interest and funding rates.
  • Fresh regulatory text or official statements.
  • Security warnings, outages, or custody changes.
  • Whether the reported developments become live products rather than announcements.

The fairest reading today is cautious attention. There are real developments in the industry, but none should be stretched into a guaranteed market direction.

items.title: Crypto Market Update: Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP Remain Flat as ETF Flows Send Mixed Signals
items.description:
The cryptocurrency market showed little movement across major assets, with Bitcoin hovering near recent support levels, Ethereum holding steady, and XRP trading within a narrow band. The lack of volatility comes as investors digest the latest ETF flow data, which showed a split between inflows and outflows across different funds. [...] According to data from [Source], Bitcoin ETFs saw net inflows of $[X] million on [Day], while Ethereum ETFs experienced net outflows of $[Y] million. This mixed picture suggests that institutional investors are not yet aligned on the near-term direction of digital assets, contributing to the subdued trading activity.

## Bitcoin: Awaiting a Catalyst [...] Bitcoin, Ethereum and XRP traded flat as mixed ETF flows—Bitcoin funds attracted inflows while Ethereum saw redemptions and XRP products showed minimal activity—keeping the market range-bound with low volume and stable crypto ETF AUM suggesting reallocations rather than exits. Traders are waiting for catalysts such as macro events, Bitcoin moving average convergence, Ethereum network upgrades and SEC clarity for XRP, so institutional behavior will be the key driver for adoption and future price

The Stablecoin Statement specifically addresses stablecoins that are designed to maintain a stable value relative to the US dollar (USD) on a one-for-one basis, [...] On September 19, 2025, Treasury issued an Advance Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (ANPRM), seeking public comment related to its implementation of the Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for U.S. Stablecoins (GENIUS) Act, a comprehensive framework for the federal regulation of payment stablecoins enacted on July 18, 2025.

Read more on Latham's Global Fintech & Digital Assets Blog. [...] On December 16, 2025, the FDIC issued a notice of proposed rulemaking (the Proposal) to implement Section 5 of the Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for US Stablecoins Act (GENIUS Act). items.title: Cryptocurrency Regulation: A Guide to U.S. & Global Policies
items.description:
Cryptocurrency regulation in the United States has historically been fragmented, with federal agencies applying different interpretations based on the nature and use of each asset. That splintered approach began to change in 2025, when Congress passed legislation to establish a clearer framework for stablecoins and digital asset markets.

## Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs [...] Cryptocurrency regulation is no longer a theoretical debate—it’s an evolving framework that is beginning to take shape worldwide. In the United States, Congress made progress in 2025 toward establishing federal oversight of stablecoins and digital asset markets. One measure—the GENIUS Act—was signed into law. [...] In the U.S., landmark legislation enacted in July 2025 has begun defining the roles of federal agencies in regulating stablecoins and digital commodities. Although implementation is ongoing, these laws represent a shift away from case-by-case enforcement and toward a structured national policy.

items.description:
